subject: Commercial readiness: procurement path & deployment preference (PO vs card, marketplace)
messages:
From: Diego Fernandez <diego@redwood.com>
To: Sylvia Holt <sylvia.holt@acmemedtech.com>
Cc: sergio_alvarez@redwood.com, neha_kapoor@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 12 May 2026 09:14:00 -0700
Subject: Commercial readiness: procurement path & deployment preference (PO vs card, marketplace)

Hi Sylvia —

Thanks again for taking the time today. Quick recap from our discovery and a few questions so we can align the commercial path before your procurement kick-off:

Notes from the call:
- Primary use: patient-facing summarization & clinical note generation (PHI).
- Traffic profile: steady daytime peaks, estimated 50 req/s at 512 tokens, 8k context for a subset.
- Compliance: SOC 2 in scope; on-prem option may be required for certain workflows.

Procurement / commercial clarifying questions:
1) Billing preference: do you plan to procure via PO/net-terms (preferred by procurement) or corporate card for initial POC?
2) Marketplace: would you prefer a marketplace purchase (AWS/Azure) or direct vendor invoicing?
3) Deployment: are you leaning Hosted (fastest), Dedicated (reserved GPUs), or Private (VPC/on-prem) for the initial contract? If PHI is required, we should mark Private/Dedicated as higher priority.
4) Commit vs on-demand: does your finance team prefer a committed-reserved capacity (monthly commit for discount) or on-demand usage billing for the pilot?

Next steps I propose:
- I’ll put together two commercial paths for procurement to review: (A) PO + Dedicated 6-month commit (PHI-ready) and (B) Card + Hosted on-demand for a 90-day pilot.
- Attach a sample SOW template and a short options sheet.
- If procurement has standard docs (W-9, 1099, vendor form) please share the point-of-contact.

Can you confirm answers to 1–4 above and share the procurement contact if different from this thread?

Best,
Diego Fernandez
Enterprise AE | Redwood Inference

From: Sylvia Holt <sylvia.holt@acmemedtech.com>
To: Diego Fernandez <diego@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@acmemedtech.com
Date: Tue, 12 May 2026 11:03:00 -04:00
Subject: Re: Commercial readiness: procurement path & deployment preference (PO vs card, marketplace)

Diego,

Thanks for the clear notes — helpful. Quick answers below and a few items from procurement: 

1) Billing preference: Procurement prefers PO with NET30 for pilots that move to production. For an initial POC they can approve a short PO (3 months) — corporate card is OK only for sandbox work.
2) Marketplace: Interested in AWS Marketplace if you can offer the same pricing and billing flow (we centralize marketplace spend). Please call out differences if any.
3) Deployment: For anything involving PHI, we will require either Dedicated or Private (on-prem/VPC). For non-PHI summarization we can start with Hosted. The team is leaning toward Dedicated for the pilot because it balances control and time-to-value.
4) Commit vs on-demand: Finance prefers a short committed term (3–6 months) for production pilots to get predictable cost into the run-rate, but procurement will accept an on-demand POC to validate integration first.

Procurement POC contact: procurement@acmemedtech.com (cc'd) — they will need your W-9 and standard insurance limits. Legal will review your standard T&Cs; I’ll share the legal reviewer contact in a separate email. Timeline: procurement can turn a PO in ~10 business days once they have vendor docs.

Sylvia Holt
Head of Clinical Product | Acme MedTech
sylvia.holt@acmemedtech.com | +1 (212) 555-9987

Diego / Neha —

Great context from Sylvia. A few internal notes and asks as we prepare the options packet for procurement:

- Pricing paths to prepare (include as separate tabs in redwood-commercial-options.pdf):
  * Option A — Dedicated (PHI): 6-month commit, monthly billing via PO, include reserved GPU pricing and baseline SLA.
  * Option B — Dedicated (PHI): 3-month pilot commit (discounted) with automatic rollover to monthly on production unless canceled.
  * Option C — Hosted (non-PHI): 90-day on-demand pilot purchasable by card or marketplace subscription.
  * Option D — Private/on-prem: enterprise licensing + professional services estimate (will need engineering intake).

- Marketplace note: include a short bullet explaining any payment flow differences (marketplace invoicing vs Redwood direct invoicing) and map to when an AWS Marketplace purchase would still allow us to meet PHI requirements (typically Dedicated in customer VPC).

- Legal/procurement asks: attach W-9 and standard insurance cert. Also include a SOW skeleton (I attached draft-sow-template.docx).

Can you draft the two-page commercial summary (A & C as priority) for Sylvia and loop procurement? I can own the discounts and margin approvals with finance.
